In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the amygdala appears to be more concerned with fear and passive avoidance, whereas the insular cortex appears to be more involved with the processing of the taste modality.
the insular (taste) cortex is involved in the processing of taste information, and the amygdala appears to be involved in the processing and storage of the affective significance of that information.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
amygdala lesions affect the motivational aspects of learning, whereas insular cortex lesions affect the cognitive aspects of learning.

the insular (and possibly the gustatory) cortex mediates taste aversion learning, whereas the amydgala mediates the reaction to the novelty and the salience of taste stimuli.

the insular and amygdaloid cortices are not functionally equivalent and that they are involved in different aspects of taste aversion learning.
